steps.text: Part 3 of 3: Before every move: two questions. This part covers Check yourself. Each part is short on purpose: finish one, play a game or take a break, and come back.

Your routine before every move: **1.** What does the last move threaten? **2.** Which of my pieces are loose? **3.** After my move, what can be taken? Capablanca names, in the notes to his own games, a time he missed an opponent's threat entirely. [I] The check is for everyone.

**Say it back.** Before I move, I ask what my opponent's last move threatens and whether any of my pieces is loose. If something is threatened I list my answers: move away, defend, capture the attacker, block, counter-attack. Then I imagine my own move and check what it leaves attacked. If nothing is threatened and nothing is loose, I carry on with my plan. After a game, I mark one moment where I was unsure.

steps.prompt: Optional, after your next game: mark one move where you were unsure. What did you think your opponent would do there? You will compare your answer with what the game shows.
